title: dedicated-autoscaler-burst-util-reporting-enhancement
author: Ava Chen
description:
Motivation: Improve Dedicated autoscaler observability and give operators finer burst controls + guaranteed throughput reporting. In a few large customers we've seen transient bursts cause confusing utilization signals and incorrect SLA routing. This change adds: 1) token-bucket smoothing knobs on the Dedicated autoscaler to reduce oscillation during short-lived traffic spikes, 2) a new throughput_guarantee metric surfaced to the fleet util reporting pipeline, and 3) per-fleet burst windows and reporting hooks so Console can show effective burst capacity vs sustained capacity.

Summary of changes: - autoscaler/tokenbucket: add smoothing param, expose current_burst_tokens, refill_rate and recent_burst_events histogram - autoscaler/controller: new heuristics to prefer short-term burst when a configured throughput_guarantee exists; improve fallback logic so canary rollouts keep SLA - observability/pipeline: emit throughput_guarantee and sustained_throughput gauges; add tag filtering for dedicated fleets - console: add a per-fleet card showing burst_capacity, sustained_capacity, and last_24h_burst_usage - docs: update dedicated autoscaling docs and add troubleshooting section for burst/noise

Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-2169) - [x] Unit + integration tests covering token-bucket smoothing - [x] End-to-end smoke test on staging with synthetic burst traffic - [x] Docs updated - [x] Metrics wired to observability pipeline

Risk/Impact: low-medium. Changes are additive and behind a feature flag (dedicated.autoscaler.burst_v46). There is a tiny behavioral change to autoscaler heuristics when throughput_guarantee is set; documented in release notes.

Notes: Kept defaults unchanged; cluster operators must opt-in to smoothing and throughput_guarantee. This addresses customer-reported incidents where short spikes tripped scaling and caused noisy utilization reporting (see SUP-4312).
